newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Bankers put up with high Philippine interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Bankers put up with high Philippine interest rates.

text.p: High Philippine interest rates are a necessary evil given the still precarious position of the peso, president of the Bankers Association of the Philippines said on Thursday.
The central bank again cut overnight interest rates on Wednesday but the borrowing rate remains a high 20 percent.

"I think the money authorities understandably have to still rely on the traditional interest rate support...under the circumstances, I think it (the rate) has gone down reasonably. We all wish it would come down faster but it is still a delicate situation," Deogracias Vistan told Reuters Financial Television.
The Philippines was forced to let the market devalue the peso two weeks ago after repeated speculative attacks began to drain its currency reserves.
On Wednesday night, central bank governor Gabriel Singson said people would have to wait "a little while" before interest rates could go back to normal levels.
Vistan said the impact on bank earnings was twin-edged.
It allowed banks to earn high yields on deposits with the central bank but also meant their depositors were choosing very short-term maturities.
Seven-day maturities were the fastest growing commodity in the banking system, reflecting the abnormal yield curve, he added.
It will take at least a month to a month-and-a-half for the market to settle down, he said.
